But towards the game: You legitimately get out of it what you put into it, pure and simple. It's not a shooter, or a space fighter sim, or an RPG, or a MMO, and it's not specifically and solely a survival crafting game. It's an exploration game with a little bit of all of that rolled into one.

No, it's not perfect, it has a couple bugs that I've found here and there. It's not ... It's not something you can easily put in a box and slap a label on, imo. I've maintained since day one that it's a niche game being marketed to a very broad audience. That's going to get a lot of negative flak right off the get-go. But it all comes down to personal preference in the end. To those that say there isn't story to drive your actions - there is, you just have to find it. You have to explore, learn, meet new aliens and learn their languages, learn what they want from you. There's plenty of stuff in there to keep you going if plain ol' imagination isn't taking you far enough. But you have to earn it, by playing the game and doing what it wants you to do: explore.

Not everyone is going to like it, obviously. It's a subjective medium. But me? I'm digging it. I'm happy with my purchase, I'm pretty invested in doing what I'm doing in it, and I'm racking up the hours. More than that, it's sticking with me in my times where I can't play it.
